cross_branch_contradictions: AI-native programming language is not one scientific variable: intent interface, canonical IR/runtime and model-native deliberative symbols are distinct mechanisms.
A model may natively generate Clay while canonical Clay semantics still require deterministic compilation, validation and authority firebreaks.
Discrete symbol purity/recurrence is not causal usefulness, emergence or proof of a literal hidden language.
Human vibe/intent is soft/ambiguous input and must not silently become canonical truth or execution authority.
One Clay semantic world reduces translation boundaries but increases common-mode failure risk; typed semantic firebreaks remain mandatory.
A bundled legacy-vs-AI-native benchmark can attribute gains to native model language that actually come from canonical IR or deterministic runtime changes.
AINL engineering evidence is strong for canonical IR/runtime architecture but does not establish C6 full-model language internalization.
AIM papers are directly relevant to endogenous symbols but remain narrow preprints and do not establish target Qwen/FRANK behavior.
fusion_target: Separate and causally connect L0 intent, L1 canonical Clay semantics, L2 learned native Clay deliberation and L3 physical neural/runtime representation; design experiments that identify benefits and failure modes per layer rather than bundling them under AI-native language.
